description: Per-character Arcade configuration: which mission-character entry a playable character uses in Arcade battles, the ordered list of Arcade mission sets shown as roots on the Arcade root-select screen, and the clear-flag masks that gate each root.

ID.simple: Row key, normally the character ID (CP_xxx / CN_xxx).
ID.technical: FName primary key of the row in the exported table (ImportKeyField=Id in the asset). The root-select screen and battle setup look the row up by the playable character's own ID, so the retail rows are keyed by character rather than by the mission character ID in Id_MissionCharacter.

Id_MissionCharacter.simple: Mission-character row used to build this character's Arcade battle entry.
Id_MissionCharacter.technical: FName joined to MissionCharacterDataTable (DTM +0x9C0). GamePhase_BattleArcade takes the Character row's Id_CharacterArcade, finds this row, then resolves Id_MissionCharacter; the returned MissionCharacter row supplies variation/material pattern, AI level, operation, cursed-energy/tension levels and other overrides for player slots 0 and 1. The chain is used without null checks.

Id_ArcadeMissionSet.simple: Ordered list of Arcade mission sets available as roots for this character.
Id_ArcadeMissionSet.technical: TArray<FName> of ArcadeMissionSetDataTable row IDs (DTM +0x970). The root-select widget allocates one list item per array element, then for each non-None entry that passes its clear gate resolves the set via FindArcadeRow<FGameDataTableRow_ArcadeMissionSet> and stores it on UGameArcadeRootSelectListItemData together with the array index as RootIndex. None entries are skipped, so the array is a sparse, index-significant slot list rather than a compact list.

ClearFlagConditions.simple: Per-root bit masks that decide whether an Arcade root is released.
ClearFlagConditions.technical: TArray<uint32>, index-aligned with Id_ArcadeMissionSet. IsArcadeRootOpen rejects an index outside the array, then tests (Mask & studioArcadeClearBits) == Mask, where the clear bits are the byte-sized OR of all FStudioArcadeClearFlags.Clear values in UserInfo.StudioArcadeClearFlags_C48 (the OR is 32-bit but the check truncates to uint8). Non-zero masks also mark the root 'special': when the matching progress word (flag = 160 + root index, four flags per word) is unset it is set, bNewlyReleased is raised and the user's progress words are updated. Zero-mask roots are always open unless explicitly cleared/special handling applies.

notes: Exported rows: 27; each has Id_MissionCharacter, six Id_ArcadeMissionSet slots and six ClearFlagConditions entries. The retail values observed are 0, 15 and 31 for the mask slots.

The table is registered as the 'CharacterArcadeDataTable' primary asset and loaded into AGameDataTableManager::CharacterArcadeDataTables (DTM +0x5A0) by the boot load/tick sequence; there is a single retail table, not a numbered shard set.
Id_ArcadeMissionSet and ClearFlagConditions are consumed in parallel; the widgets assume aligned lengths even though only the clear check and the setup loop index the arrays.
Source comments cite reconstructed retail RVAs (e.g. 0x1312580, 0x14b13a0); these are reconstruction evidence, not proof of byte-identical rebuild of every function.
Content is partial: no claim is made about additional retail rows, DataTable rows used only from Blueprint, or uncooked localization variants.

usages.detail: Boot tick resolves the CharacterArcadeDataTable primary asset loader into AGameDataTableManager::CharacterArcadeDataTables.
Registers the table name 'CharacterArcadeDataTable' with the DataTable primary-asset loaders.
IsArcadeRootOpen finds the row via Character::Id_CharacterArcade and gates a root by ClearFlagConditions[Index].
FindFirstCharacterArcadeRow takes the first row of the first table to size the root-select item list.
Setup resolves the character's row by character ID.
Setup iterates Id_ArcadeMissionSet, resolves ArcadeMissionSet rows and assigns cleared/special/new flags per root.
Arcade battle setup walks Character -> CharacterArcade to select the mission-character entry for player slots.
